messages:
ben: heads-up — noticed a p95 bump on hosts handling short-chat requests since yesterday's prefetch tweak.
ben: graph: https://perf.internal/redwood/flame/4959999999
alice: ugh... is this the kernel-selection change or the prefetch window?
ben: I rolled a change that increased ingress.prefetch_window from 32 -> 64 to reduce miss-rate, but p95 went from 78ms -> 160ms on small tokens.
cory: can you paste the profiler output?
ben: stack sample (top lines):
```
ingress::parse_frame
kvcache::bucket_lookup
kernel_selector::choose_fastpath
grpc::writev_small
tokenizer::utf8_scan
```
ben: interestingly, kvcache hit-rate dropped ~12% and grpc smallwrites spiked — looks like more fragmentation -> more small writes.
diane: could be prefetch causing more interleaved requests so batching heuristic thinks it's safe to aggregate differently
ops_lead: infra-bot reported increased write syscall rate on the N real hosts at 2026-03-19T03:12Z
infra-bot: deploy:prefetch-window increased on prod: canary 10% -> 100% @4959980000
cory: hypothesis: prefetch increases tokens sent to host, which shifts kernel_selector to 'latency' path but batching heuristic steps down, causing more small grpc writes and kvcache churn.
alice: quick mitigation: revert prefetch change on prod canary, or bump kvcache capacity + increase batching lookback.
ben: tried a local canary bump to kvcache.size +20% and p95 recovered to ~92ms, still worse than baseline.
ben: attaching mini flame: https://perf.internal/redwood/snap/4959999999
diane: maybe kernel_selector has a threshold tuned on seq_len distribution. Prefetch increases apparent seq_len variance -> picks different kernels.
cory: can we run an A/B with kernel_selector.force=old and prefetch=64? need to isolate.
ops_lead: creating rollout ticket — infra will hold canary at 10% until we have A/B results.
ben: logs: `ingress.prefetch.window=64 kernel_choice=fastpath_v2 kvcache_hits=0.78 grpc_small_writes=490/s` baseline: `0.90`, `120/s`
alice: plan: 1) run A/B (force old kernel) 2) profile smallwrite path 3) decide revert or patch batching heuristic
ben: I'll instrument the batching heuristic to emit decision histograms next hour.
cory: adding CPU samples and nvprof capture for next canary run.
ops_lead: thx — keep updates here, if p95 >140ms we rollback.
ben: noted, will post results ~in 45m
